 By Ira Winderman | iwinderman@sunsentinel.com | South Florida Sun Sentinel PUBLISHED: October 29, 2026 at 6:05 AM EDT | UPDATED: October 29, 2026 at 8:53 AM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Q: Klay Thompson. Ira, that is my question. Go. – Sid. 
 A: Look, we’ve chronicled that Klay Thompson has been a slow starter at times, that October has been the worst shooting month of his career. So in that regard, the Heat only have one game left this month. So there’s that. But yes, this has fallen far short of expectation amid this small sample size. Wednesday night in Atlanta , he was limited to opening stints of both halves, 17:02 total, closing 1 of 4 from the field, all on 3-pointers. The reality is that with the way he and Tim Hardaway Jr. are defending, the Heat may not be able to have a designated shooter on the floor at closing time, at least in the games they’re playing from the lead.

 Q:  A work in progress. I saw it the last three games and then we put one together.  Now we move on with intentions to keep getting better and winning. OK Bam Adebayo haters, you can jump back on the wagon.  It’s OK. We don’t hold grudges over here. – Doug. 
 A: It’s almost as if the 0-4 also was a wake-up call for Erik Spoelstra. There was a far greater degree of comfort offense, getting back to more pick-and-roll and dribble handoffs. With this roster, that is what can work best when you absolutely need to get a basket. Yes, the pace can be fun. But at clutch time, pace also can be dangerous (just ask Pelle Larsson and his ill-fated homerun pass gone awry to Bam Adebayo). When you don’t have a team with a perimeter closer, when you lack a wing who can create his own offense, a systematic approach often is the best approach. So pick, roll, handoff, get traditional, even if it seems too formulaic. Formulaic can be just fine when it gets your players in their best scoring spots.
 Q: This must have been the worst start in Heat history. So much promise turned into so much disappointment.  – Bob, Davie. 
 A: Um, well there was that 0-17 start to their inaugural season in 1988-89. Yes, it was an expansion year with minimal expectations. But not so minimal that it would take so long to get a victory before the Clippers were kind enough.
